headline: Evaluation design and context choices are tested as drivers of apparent predictive gains
label: Validation Design In Predictive Models
summary: Four preprints probe whether time-context, partitioning and feature-view choices, not model architecture, account for reported gains in clinical and CRISPR prediction.
synthesis: The shared thread is scrutiny of design choices that shape reported performance. An EHR transformer for colorectal cancer prediction finds that gains plateau at about 18 years of time-context, with RoPE aliasing beyond roughly 20 years. A re-evaluation across 13 TCGA cancers shows that test-set selection and partition variance can rival reported concordance gains in cross-cancer survival prediction. TriCasRank for Cas12a crRNA activity ranking asks when ensembling helps and when context matters more, using fold-internal historical summaries. A hierarchical temporal transformer on pathology reports tests visit timing and transfer to unseen TCGA tumour types. What is new is the explicit quantification of context length and evaluation variance as confounders of model comparison.
